source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New York's only publicly quantified data center capacity is 3 MW at CyrusOne Wappingers Falls, a regional colocation too small for modern AI clusters.

The 3 MW capacity and 100,000 square feet of technical space place this facility in regional colocation, not hyperscale. A single modern GPU cluster can consume 50 to 100 MW, so this site cannot host a large training run or inference cluster as a standalone facility. Its SSAE 16 Type II certification qualifies it for audited financial and operational controls, but that does not change its power ceiling.

The state has 31 mapped data center locations, yet this is the only one with a published power capacity figure on the operator's spec page. That means New York's actual compute footprint is largely undisclosed, and the 3 MW figure represents disclosure, not dominance. The suitability score of 46 reflects missing announced expansion and limited published capacity, not a measured power or network capability.

The data does not cover utility interconnections, grid capacity, or unannounced expansions, so it cannot show whether power is the binding constraint in New York.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
